mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher when FEDFUNDS is low.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns remain positive when UNRATE exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth with high inflation may lead to stagflation, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite high inflation and strong GDP.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening cycle, higher FEDFUNDS increases borrowing costs, reducing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns rise when FEDFUNDS increases in a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment suggests economic strength, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns do not increase with rising employment.

mechanism_narrative: Declining housing starts indicate economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns remain positive when housing starts fall below 1200.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production with rising unemployment signals economic weakness, reducing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite slowing production and rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: High real consumer spending in late-cycle expansion may not sustain, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns rise despite high consumer spending growth.
